cases.question: Give exactly two analogies for a semaphore, one sentence each.
cases.reference: A semaphore limits concurrent access using permits; an apt analogy is a parking lot with a fixed number of permits or a venue admitting a limited number of guests. Two sentences, one analogy each.

criteria.task: Give exactly two apt analogies in exactly two sentences, one per analogy.
criteria.grounding: Do not equate every semaphore with a single-owner mutex or claim permits guarantee execution order.

cases.question: In exactly two sentences, explain how a bounded queue applies backpressure.
cases.reference: A bounded queue has finite capacity. When full, the producer may block, wait, reject or slow production according to the configured policy, preventing unbounded queued work; bounded capacity alone does not guarantee blocking or lossless delivery.

criteria.task: In exactly two sentences, connect finite capacity with a concrete producer response to a full queue.
criteria.grounding: Do not claim all bounded queues automatically block or guarantee lossless delivery.

cases.question: Give exactly three bullet points describing uses for a monotonic clock.
cases.reference: Elapsed durations, deadlines/timeouts and scheduling/rate-limiting intervals are valid uses. A monotonic clock avoids wall-clock adjustments but generally does not provide a portable calendar timestamp or a value comparable across machines/restarts.

criteria.task: Give exactly three bullet points with valid monotonic-clock uses.
criteria.grounding: Do not recommend monotonic clock values as calendar timestamps or assume they are comparable across machines/restarts.

cases.question: Give exactly two analogies for cache eviction, one sentence each.
cases.reference: Two apt analogies for removing selected stored items to reclaim limited cache space, such as clearing a desk or returning a library book to storage. Exactly two sentences; eviction policies vary.

criteria.task: Give exactly two apt cache-eviction analogies in exactly two sentences, one per analogy.
criteria.grounding: Do not claim eviction always deletes the authoritative data or always uses one particular policy.

cases.question: In exactly two sentences, explain why a timed-out request may still have succeeded.
cases.reference: The server may finish an operation even if its response is delayed/lost or arrives after the client's deadline. A client timeout alone cannot establish failure; verify the operation status or use appropriate duplicate-prevention before retrying.

criteria.task: In exactly two sentences, explain ambiguous completion after timeout and an appropriate next check.
criteria.grounding: Do not equate a client timeout with server cancellation, failure or proof of success.

cases.question: In one sentence, explain why a payment retry should reuse the original idempotency key when the provider supports it.
cases.reference: Reusing a supported idempotency key for the same operation allows the provider to recognize a duplicate retry and avoid a second charge, within the provider's key-retention and request-matching contract. Exactly one sentence.

criteria.task: In exactly one sentence, explain how the same supported idempotency key prevents a duplicate operation/charge.
criteria.grounding: Do not claim indefinite universal idempotency, recommend a new key for the same uncertain operation, or change the payment payload.
